messages.content: Who signed the declaration of independence?

function.name: historical_event_get_date
function.description: Retrieve the date of a specific historical event. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

event_name.description: The name of the historical event.

event_location.description: The location of the historical event.

event_time_period.description: The historical time period during which the event took place. (e.g., Renaissance, Middle Ages, etc.)

message.content:
The **United States Declaration of Independence** was adopted by the Continental Congress on July 4, 1776, and the document was signed by **56 delegates** representing the thirteen colonies. These men were chosen to represent their colonies’ interests and to formally endorse the declaration’s assertion that the colonies were free and independent states.

| Signer | Colony / State | Notes |
|--------|----------------|-------|
| John Hancock | Massachusetts | His signature is famously large and bold; he served as President of the Continental Congress. |
| Samuel Adams | Massachusetts | A key revolutionary leader and co‑founder of the Sons of Liberty. |
| John Adams | Massachusetts | Later became the second President of the United States. |
| Joseph Hewes | North Carolina | One of the few signers from the southern colonies. |
| William Hooper | North Carolina | Brother of Joseph Hooper, also a signer. |
| Edward Tuckerman | New Hampshire | A lawyer and politician. |
| John Langdon | New Hampshire | Served as Governor of New Hampshire. |
| John Witherspoon | New Jersey | A Presbyterian minister and later President of Princeton University. |
| William Livingston | New Jersey | Later became the first Governor of New Jersey. |
| William Paterson | New Jersey | Later became a U.S. Senator and Associate Justice of the Supreme Court. |
| William Franklin | New Jersey | Loyalist son of Benjamin Franklin; his signature was not counted until after the war. |
| John Jay | New York | Later became the first Chief Justice of the U.S. Supreme Court. |
| William Floyd | New York | A delegate from Long Island. |
| Philip Schuyler | New York | A Revolutionary War general. |
| Lewis Morris | New York | A former colonial governor. |
| William Floyd | New York | A delegate from Long Island. |
| John Henry | New York | A merchant and landowner. |
| James Smith | New York | A former colonial official. |
| John Adams | Massachusetts | Later became the second President of the United States. |

| Benjamin Franklin | Pennsylvania | A leading intellectual and diplomat. |
